answer: An agent marketplace requires a locked bond for each unit of bidding weight, so splitting one operator into a thousand identities gives no extra influence without extra capital. Whether an agent tends a garden, detects an ember, or appraises a relic, its bond stays locked through a dispute window and is slashed for cryptographically proven double billing. A sybil swarm therefore ties up funds proportional to its influence and risks losing them when it cheats.
